discoveredCase: Host ports are ephemeral and bound to loopback; readiness means the service answers
behaviorContract: Every published port is written as 127.0.0.1::<container port> so Docker assigns a free loopback port per run and publishes it atomically; the runner asks Docker afterwards which ports were bound. Every healthcheck asserts usable service, not a started process: RabbitMQ checks running plus port connectivity because the setup creates the test vhost over HTTP; ActiveMQ checks that Jolokia answers with status 200; SQL Server runs SELECT 1; PostgreSQL runs pg_isready; Artemis dials its own container name because the acceptor does not bind loopback; the HAProxy check deliberately only proves it is listening, because whether anything is behind it is what the outage changes.

assertionIntent: Prevents port collisions, prevents publishing a test broker on every host interface, and prevents a run starting against a service that is up but not usable.
notes: Successor: Testcontainers wait strategies. Each of the six readiness definitions is a separate promise; a generic port-open wait is weaker than five of them. PostgreSQL keeps its data directory in tmpfs so no stale volume can survive with an earlier run's credentials. The ActiveMQ image carries exactly one delta against the official configuration, schedulerSupport=true, which DelayRetry_Specs needs; groups.properties binds vicione_ci to the admins role so the run account is not refused with HTTP 403.
